newsitem.title: TURKEY: Libya failure takes Turkey's Erbakan to low point.
newsitem.headline: Libya failure takes Turkey's Erbakan to low point.

text.p: Turkey's divided opposition on Tuesday turned on beleaguered Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for Islamist foreign policy failures that have dragged his three-month-old government to its lowest point.
Adding to Erbakan's woes, Turkey's closest ally Washington finally ran out of patience over his flirtations with radical Moslem states.
A left-wing party said it would greet Erbakan on his return from a controversial African tour later in the day with a censure motion to topple the Islamist-led coalition.
"Our nation has not fallen into such humiliation in its foreign relations since it was founded," the leftist Republican People's Party (CHP) said in a written request to parliament.
CHP deputy Nihat Matkap said his party had asked parliament on Monday to take up the censure motion. MPs must debate it within two weeks.

The opposition and the media have slammed Erbakan for a visit to Libya at the weekend. Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi strongly criticised Turkey's treatment of its Kurds and its ties to the West at a joint news conference with Erbakan on Sunday.
It was the worst of several rebuffs for Erbakan in a bid to take NATO-member Turkey closer to the Moslem and Arab world.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist premier, has five deputies more than the 276 needed to win a censure vote in the 550-seat assembly. But some MPs in the pro-Western True Path Party (DYP) government ally are uneasy at his foreign efforts.

Interior Minister Mehmet Agar had threatened to resign if Erbakan went to Libya, under U.N. sanctions for refusing to hand over two suspects in the bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland in 1988.
Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, the DYP's leader, accused Libya and two of Turkey's Moslem neighbours of sponsoring Kurdish guerrillas in Turkey.
"Whether it be Libya, Iran or Syria, they support terrorism in Turkey," Anatolian news agency quoted her as saying.
But Ciller, facing corruption charges that Erbakan has so far stalled, fell short of directly criticising the prime minister's foreign policy.
The United States has delivered an uncharacteristic "stiff rebuke" to Turkey over the Libya visit.
"You can't just go to another country and meet a dictator and absolve him of all responsibility for a terrorist act," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Monday.
He said the department was still checking the accuracy of media reports quoting Erbakan as saying that Libya was "against terrorist activities" and was "the country suffering most from terror".
"It's up to allies to be good allies and to understand you can't pick and choose places where you're going to support us or not support us," Burns said on Monday.

Washington, keen to promote Turkey as a democratic partner in an unstable region, strongly backs Ankara against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels despite alleged human rights abuses by Turkish forces.

The United States refrained from punishing Turkey for signing a $23-billion gas deal with Tehran in August that sailed close to violating a U.S. law forbidding foreign companies investing in energy projects in Iran.
